comparator.name: Media and Information
comparator.sourceNotes: The first year is common to both specialisations. This comparison shows Cultural Information Studies, the first listed specialisation. The second year includes 36 EC of specialisation courses and 24 EC of common methods and philosophy. Year three includes 42 EC of open electives and the 18 EC research seminar and thesis.

components.name: Living Information
components.note: The first year also includes an uncredited Academic Literacy Test and tutoring. Tutoring continues in the later years.

components.name: Media Research
components.note: Includes academic writing and builds on introductory digital-culture and media study.

components.name: Digital Methods and Information Analytics
components.note: Requires positive binding study advice. Analysing Digital Culture and Doing Media Studies 2 are recommended preparation.

components.name: Philosophy of the Humanities 2 (Media and Information)
components.note: Builds on the first Philosophy of the Humanities course, offered earlier in the semester.

components.name: Introduction to Digital Humanities
components.note: The first Cultural Information Studies course introduces digital humanities research. The guide recommends prior introductory digital culture and media study.

components.name: Archives, Information and Society
components.note: Studies archival principles, practices and their connections to power, identity and institutions.

components.name: Coding the Humanities
components.note: Builds on Introduction to Digital Humanities and applies Python to cultural data and questions.

components.name: Data-Driven Research & Digital Humanities Lab
components.note: Builds on Introduction to Digital Humanities and Coding the Humanities and assumes basic Python.

components.name: Free-choice electives, minor, internship or study abroad
components.note: The regulations allocate 30 EC of open electives in the first semester and 12 EC in the second. Options include a minor, electives, mobility or a placement, subject to the programme rules.

components.name: Research Seminar and Bachelor's Thesis Media and Information
components.note: Pass the compulsory first- and second-year courses before entry. Archives, Information and Society is exempt from the entry requirement for this specialisation.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three options address digital media and data, cultural information and historical interpretation, or public communication and digital strategy. Their different course groups support distinct purposes.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop programming in Python. UCR teaches general computational problem-solving, while UvA applies code to cultural objects and data.
Both collect and analyse digital data. UCR teaches a general R workflow. UvA applies digital methods to media and information research.
Both use concepts to analyse media forms and practices. UCR emphasises film form and media history.
Both examine how media technologies change and shape cultural practice. UCR uses historical objects and infrastructures.
Both develop research design and qualitative interpretation. UCR uses interviews, ethnography and other social-science methods. UvA applies research to media cases.

notes.text: UCR combines media and cultural study with computing, social research or public communication. UvA provides a dedicated sequence in digital methods, archival studies and coding for the humanities, with an 18 EC research seminar and thesis. Its other specialisation concentrates on new media and digital culture.

audience.programmeDescription: Media and Information at the University of Amsterdam studies how digital media and information shape culture and society. The Cultural Information Studies specialisation focuses on archives, digital humanities and data-driven research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related options in digital media and data, cultural information and historical research, or media and public communication. UvA gives more sustained attention to digital-media research and ends with a required research seminar and thesis.
